papers.title: Installing multifunctionality on titanium with RGD-decorated polyurethane-polyurea roxithromycin loaded nanoparticles: toward new osseointegrative therapies.
papers.abstract: A novel class of polyurethane-polyurea nanoparticles (PUUa NPs) to install multifunctionality on biomaterials is presented. Biofunctionalization of titanium with roxithromycin loaded RGD-decorated PUUa NPs results in an outstanding improvement of osteoblast adhesion and strong suppression of bacterial attachment. This strategy represents a powerful approach to enhance the osseointegration of implant materials.

summary_en.method: RGD-decorated polyurethane-polyurea nanoparticles loaded with roxithromycin were deposited on titanium substrates.

papers.title: Microfabrication of scaffold-free tissue strands for three-dimensional tissue engineering
papers.abstract: In this note, we report a practical and efficient method based on a coaxial extrusion and microinjection technique for biofabrication of scaffold-free tissue strands. Tissue strands were obtained using tubular alginate conduits as mini-capsules with well-defined permeability and mechanical properties, where their removal by ionic decrosslinking allowed the formation of scaffold-free cell aggregates in the form of cylindrical strands with well-defined morphology and geometry. Rat dermal fibroblasts and mouse insulinoma beta TC3 cells were used to fabricate both single-cellular and heterocellular tissue strands with high cell viability, self-assembling capability and the ability to express cell-specific functional markers. By taking advantage of tissue self-assembly, we succeeded in guiding the fusion of tissue strands to fabricate larger tissue patches. The presented approach enables fabrication of cell aggregates with controlled dimensions allowing highly long strands, which can be used for various applications, including fabrication of scale-up complex tissues and of tissue models for drug screening and cancer studies.

summary_en.motivation: To develop a practical method for fabricating scaffold-free tissue strands with controlled dimensions for tissue engineering applications.
summary_en.method: Coaxial extrusion and microinjection were used to create tubular alginate capsules as templates, which were removed by ionic decrosslinking to yield scaffold-free cell aggregates.
summary_en.result: Single-cellular and heterocellular tissue strands with high viability, self-assembly capability, and functional marker expression were obtained, and fusion of strands into larger patches was demonstrated.
summary_en.validation: In vitro experiments with rat dermal fibroblasts and mouse insulinoma beta TC3 cells confirmed cell viability, morphology, and functional markers.
